rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (the best so far, score 122.0): every trial on all three tracks ended off_track, and max_error sat at about 0.0625 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Oval progress rose to 0.63 with one finish in 20 trials, but s-bend progress was 0.095 and slalom progress 0.07. The s-bend had no line loss, so the robot drifted off the outside of bends while still seeing the tape. The slalom had one line loss, which means the tape left the outermost sensors (x = +/-0.06 m, footprint about 0.012 m). Steering oscillation is low (0.11 to 0.33), so the controller is not jittering. It is under-steering on curves, and the sensor span is too narrow for the larger lateral excursions. Changes: (1) widen the array to 7 sensors spanning x = +0.075 to -0.075 m at 0.025 m spacing, so the tape stays visible at larger offsets and the centroid signal has finer resolution; (2) weights become [2, 1.33, 0.67, 0, -0.67, -1.33, -2], which keeps the signal range at +/-2 and the same overall gain per metre of offset; (3) kp rises from 2.5 to 3.0 for more steering authority on bends; (4) kd stays at 0.6 to damp the extra gain; (5) base_speed drops from 1.6 to 1.5, which gives more time to correct on tight bends and still meets the roughly 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s. Expected result: fewer off-track exits on the s-bend and slalom, a line loss count of 0 or near 0, and progress above 0.5 on all tracks. Hypotheses: (a) if s-bend progress stays under 0.3 with max_error near 0.06, the bends need more kp or less speed; (b) if steering_oscillation rises above 0.4, kd should go up or kp back down; (c) if the robot completes with completion_time above 3 s, base_speed should rise toward 1.7. Body width is kept at 0.12 m, because widening it to 0.18 m only lifts the off-track limit to about 0.0575 m, which is not worth the change.
